sec: Sepsis: pathophysiology, causes and clinical features · p800

items.q: Complete the sepsis pathophysiology flowchart — 1) Pre-renal component  2) Macrovascular change  3) Microvascular change … A) Predominant over ATN  B) Microthrombi + endothelial leak  C) Widespread systemic vasodilation
items.exp: Sepsis flowchart: pre-renal (predominant) >> ATN; widespread systemic vasodilation (macrovascular) + microthrombi + endothelial leak (microvascular) → ↓↓ kidney perfusion. (Book p800)

items.q: In sepsis, the pre-renal component predominates over ATN, and microthrombi with endothelial leak cause ↓↓ kidney perfusion.
opts: False — ATN predominates from the outset
False — there is no pre-renal component in sepsis
True, but only in fungal sepsis
items.exp: Sepsis flowchart: pre-renal (predominant) >> ATN, with vasodilation plus microthrombi and endothelial leak reducing kidney perfusion. (Book p800)

items.q: Match the sepsis ATN pathway — 1) ↑PAMPs, DAMPs  2) Next step  3) Result … A) Inflammatory cascade  B) Released in ATN  C) Oxidative stress
items.exp: ATN arm of the sepsis flowchart: ↑PAMPs, DAMPs → inflammatory cascade → oxidative stress. (Book p800)

items.q: Match the causes of sepsis-associated AKI — 1) Urosepsis  2) CRBSI  3) Diabetic nephropathy with soft tissue infection (cellulitis) … A) Urosepsis  B) Catheter related bloodstream infection  C) Cellulitis
items.exp: Causes of sepsis in this section: urosepsis; CRBSI (catheter related blood stream infection); DM nephropathy with soft tissue infection (cellulitis); also renal allograft recipients, UTI and post-operative patients. (Book p800)

items.q: The sepsis causes listed besides urosepsis, CRBSI and cellulitis are:
opts: Renal allograft recipients, UTI and post-operative state
Cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome and heart failure
items.exp: Causes list: urosepsis, CRBSI, DM nephropathy with soft tissue infection (cellulitis), renal allograft recipients, UTI and post-operative. (Book p800)

items.q: In early sepsis, why may the skin feel warm despite poor end-organ perfusion?
opts: Because blood flow is redirected, so the skin is warm in the early phase (cool skin later)
Because the patient is febrile from the infection only
items.exp: Signs of poor end-organ perfusion: HR >90/min, cool skin (redirection of blood flow) — warm in the early phase — with ↓urine output and restlessness. (Book p800)

items.q: Match each sign of poor end-organ perfusion in sepsis — 1) Heart rate  2) Skin  3) Urine output  4) Sensorium … A) ↓  B) Restlessness  C) >90/min  D) Cool skin (warm early)
items.exp: Sepsis clinical features (signs of poor end-organ perfusion): HR >90/min; cool skin (redirection of blood flow), warm in the early phase; ↓urine output; restlessness. (Book p800)

items.q: The heart-rate threshold given among the signs of poor end-organ perfusion in sepsis is:
items.exp: Signs of poor end-organ perfusion: HR >90/min, plus cool skin, ↓urine output and restlessness. (Book p800)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed as causes of sepsis-related AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Listed causes: urosepsis, CRBSI, DM nephropathy with soft tissue infection (cellulitis), renal allograft recipients, UTI and post-operative state. (Book p800)
